content.text: FAQHow to invest in Anduril?Anduril is a privately held company. Only accredited and institutional investors can invest in privately held companies before their IPO. Investors seeking exposure to pre-IPO companies such as Anduril can invest via special purpose vehicles, funds, investment syndicates, or, purchase shares directly depending on the company's policy on stock transferability.Can you buy Anduril stock?Due to regulations, only accredited and institutional investors are eligible to purchase the stock of private companies like Anduril. Even then, most direct stock transfers must be approved by Anduril itself. Some companies do not generally approve transfers of common shares. In such companies, investors might be able to get exposure to the company by investing indirectly through a fund or special purpose vehicle.Can you sell Anduril shares before it goes public?If you own Anduril shares, you may be able to find a buyer on pre-IPO marketplaces or through a registered broker. Whether you can sell your shares ultimately depends on several factors such as the class of shares you own, the holding period prescribed by regulations, if applicable, and Anduril's stance on share transfers as laid out in option agreements, option plans, company bylaws, shareholder agreements, or other company documents.Want to learn more? Read this guide to selling pre-IPO shares and frequently asked questions.What is Anduril's stock price?As a privately held company, Anduril has no public stock price. To access current and historical pricing information on Anduril stock, you can review filings from the company's past primary funding rounds, fund marks, and information from secondary trading data providers. Hiive also offers free access to historical trading data on hundreds of the top pre-IPO companies such as Anduril, based on its platform activity.What is the valuation of Anduril?The valuation of private companies such as Anduril is not readily available because they are not listed on public exchanges.One source of information on Anduril's valuation is the details of its most recent primary funding rounds. Financial and technology news sources such as Reuters, Bloomberg, Techcrunch, and The Information routinely report on private company funding rounds and can be a good source of information. Alternatively, you can look at Anduril's official website for press releases and investor relations updates, alongside venture capital databases such as Crunchbase, Pitchbook, and Preqin.Is Anduril publicly traded?Anduril remains a privately held company and cannot be accessed on major public exchanges such as NASDAQ or NYSE.Accredited investors can invest in the top private companies like Anduril before they IPO via secondary marketplaces such as Hiive.Disclaimer: Nothing in this FAQ represents an offer to buy or sell, or a solicitation of an offer to buy or sell, any security.
